STEP 1 - Scene: A small side salad of mixed leafy greens (lettuce/spring mix) with shredded carrot and a few dark pieces (possibly red cabbage or dried fruit/nut bits), lightly dressed. No main course visible.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square/rounded plate, roughly 22 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm^2 (treating it as a round-equivalent).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Mixed leafy greens (lettuce, mixed leaves)
- Shredded carrot
- Dark shredded vegetable (red cabbage or similar), small amount
- Light dressing residue (not clearly visible, minor)

STEP 4 - Area (percent of vessel area):
- Mixed leafy greens: ~13% of vessel (~50 cm^2)
- Shredded carrot: ~1% (~4 cm^2)
- Red cabbage/dark shreds: ~1% (~4 cm^2)
Food covers roughly 15% of the plate; the rest is empty.

STEP 5 - Volume (gross envelope):
- Leafy greens: 50 cm^2 x 3 cm ≈ 150 ml
- Carrot: 4 cm^2 x 0.5 cm ≈ 2 ml
- Red cabbage: 4 cm^2 x 0.5 cm ≈ 2 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Leafy greens: 150 ml x 0.15 ≈ 23 g
- Carrot: 2 ml x 0.6 ≈ 1 g
- Red cabbage: 2 ml x 0.5 ≈ 1 g
Total ≈ 25 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Leafy greens: 23 g x 20 kcal/100 g ≈ 5 kcal
- Carrot: 1 g x 40 kcal/100 g ≈ 0.4 kcal
- Red cabbage: 1 g x 25 kcal/100 g ≈ 0.3 kcal
Total ≈ 6 kcal (dressing not visibly present in quantity; if a dressing was used, add roughly 30–60 kcal).

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A modest pile of greens with a few carrot shreds on a large plate should weigh tens of grams, not hundreds. About 25 g and under 10 kcal of visible food is plausible; I'll keep the estimate at the visible food only.
